functions.title: Codex of Chaos
pages:
Codex of Chaos

A field guide to Kael'Vorr, the Demon Lord, the Demon Altar, and inventions that should never have worked.

Kael'Vorr

He has crossed countless dimensions collecting creatures, materials, energies, and ideas. Every impossible encounter is a question waiting to be asked.

The Overworld

Its forests grew normally, oceans followed rules, and even monsters fit a natural order. Kael'Vorr admired that stability until admiration became boredom.

The Experiment

He introduced pieces of other realities: a living infection, a demonic hellscape, bodiless flesh, altered predators, and trees born under alien laws.

His Question

Where others see danger, Kael'Vorr sees possibility:

What happens when this meets something it was never meant to encounter?

The Demon Lord

A ruler taken from a collapsing infernal realm. Kael'Vorr did not enslave it. He gave it a door, an audience, and reasons to keep fighting.

Hell Brutes

Living siege engines shaped by pressure, rage, and demon steel. They protect territory by turning every approach into a test of endurance.

Emberstalkers

Hunters adapted to ash and flame. They follow heat, movement, and fear with equal patience.

Demon Drops

Demon Ash, Demon Hearts, Demon Steel, and Corrupted XP are the working materials of infernal craft.

Corrupted XP

Experience remembers action. The altar twists that memory into physical power, producing Corrupted XP Orbs from a successful sacrifice.

Demon Altar

Craft the first altar with Demon Ash, Demon Steel Ingots, a Demon Heart, and a Nether Star. Power it with redstone while a sacrifice stands upon it.

Altar Function

A powered altar sacrifices the creature above it and converts nearby experience into Corrupted XP Orbs. It no longer spreads corruption into terrain.

Ritual Blocks

Demon Skulls and Demon Pentagrams are crafted from demon drops. They are also keys to calling the Demon Lord.

Lord Ritual

Build vertically:
  Skull
Skull Pentagram Skull
  Pentagram

Completing the five blocks consumes them and summons the Demon Lord.

Corrupted Star

The Demon Lord has a rare chance to drop a Corrupted Nether Star. It is the core catalyst for forced altar upgrades.

Altar Tier II

Combine a Tier I altar with a Corrupted Nether Star, Demon Ash, Demon Hearts, and Demon Steel in its Chaos crafting tier.

Altar Tier III

Upgrade Tier II using another Corrupted Nether Star, ash, hearts, Corrupted XP, and Demon Steel.

Altar Tier IV

Upgrade Tier III with two Corrupted Nether Stars, ash, hearts, blood-flesh blocks, and a Corrupted XP Block.

Altar Tier V

The rarest altar requires Tier IV, four Corrupted Nether Stars, two Demon Hearts, and a Corrupted XP Block.

Chaos Weapons

Demon steel remembers violence. Infected crystal adapts. Living flesh repairs. Corrupted experience supplies raw intent. Kael'Vorr forced them to coexist.

Unfinished Work

Every Chaos Weapon is unstable and partly alive. Its wielder's health, emotion, and action may change how it behaves.

F = Demon Flesh material

The Inventor

Kael'Vorr may help heroes defeat an experiment, then improve that same creature and release it elsewhere. Results matter more than sides.

Final Note

Creation without risk is decoration. Let us make something uncertain.

—Kael'Vorr

functions.title: Emberstalker Notes
pages:
Emberstalker Notes

Observations from the ash paths where flame learned patience.

Origin

Emberstalkers came from a realm without sunrise. Heat moved through black dust like weather, and predators learned to follow it.

The Collection

Kael'Vorr watched one stalk a cooling meteor for nine days. He opened a gate before it reached the crater.

In the Overworld

Here, every torch, furnace, and living body is a bright trail. The creature finds this abundance delightful.

Behavior

An Emberstalker is faster than its silhouette suggests. Open ground favors the hunter; barriers and prepared terrain favor you.

Ash

Its Demon Ash is not ordinary soot. It carries a weak memory of the fire that made it.

Heart

A Demon Heart is rare because most infernal bodies burn theirs completely. An intact one can stabilize impossible crafting.

Corrupted XP

Some Emberstalkers carry experience warped by dimensional travel. The substance is valuable at a Demon Altar.

Chaos Keys

A very rare kill may produce a Chaos Key, proof that Kael'Vorr occasionally hides rewards inside the danger itself.

Altar Use

Power a Demon Altar with redstone while a sacrifice stands above it. The altar converts released experience into Corrupted XP Orbs.

Crafting

Ash, hearts, and demon steel form the foundation of Chaos gear. Higher altar tiers reveal stronger recipes.

functions.title: Anatomy of a Brute
pages:
Anatomy of a Brute

A practical guide to the infernal siege creature called the Hell Brute.

Origin

Hell Brutes guarded fortresses in a realm where walls grew back. Their answer was to become stronger than regeneration.

Selection

Kael'Vorr chose them because they solve problems without changing methods. He considers this limitation scientifically useful.

Body

Dense flesh surrounds a furnace-hot core. Demon steel fragments grow through the body like a second skeleton.

Temperament

A Brute is not mindless. It simply considers subtlety an inefficient distance between itself and a target.

Combat

Keep space, use terrain, and never assume one stagger has ended its charge. A Brute's momentum is part of the weapon.

Demon Ash

Brutes shed more ash than Emberstalkers. Their constant internal heat consumes tissue even while they fight.

Demon Hearts

Their hearts are rare, durable catalysts used throughout demon crafting and Chaos Altar recipes.

Corrupted XP

The Brute can drop Corrupted XP Orbs. A powered Demon Altar can also make them from sacrifices.

Demon Skull

Craft with Demon Ash, Bone Blocks, and a Demon Heart. Three skulls are required in the Demon Lord ritual.

Pentagram

Craft with Demon Ash, Redstone, and a Demon Heart. Two pentagrams complete the ritual frame.

Lord Ritual

functions.author: Kael'Vorr
functions.title: The Lesser Flame
pages:
The Lesser Flame

Field notes on Imps: small demons whose size has never limited their appetite for trouble.

Origin

Imps nested in the vents beneath infernal citadels. They survived larger demons through speed, numbers, and knowing every escape route.

The Collection

Kael'Vorr found an entire colony dismantling one of his instruments. He admired their curiosity before noticing they had stolen the screws.

Behavior

An Imp attacks whatever it sees as vulnerable. Once one gives chase, its wings and claws make losing it difficult.

Stronghold Nests

Demon Strongholds use enchanted cages to replenish their Imp population. Libraries, guarded doors, and treasure chambers are common nesting sites.

Combat

Imps are tougher and stronger than common zombies. Fight them before a spawner fills the room, and do not let their size hide their reach.

Fire

Infernal heat does not harm them. Fire and lava are shelter to an Imp, not obstacles.

Demon Ash

Their bodies leave small quantities of useful Demon Ash. Rare specimens preserve a Demon Heart or Corrupted XP Orb.

Chaos Keys

An Imp may carry a Chaos Key stolen from somewhere more important. This is rare, but theft makes them surprisingly effective couriers.

Lord Ritual

Place vertically:
  Skull
Skull Pentagram Skull
  Pentagram

Completing the cross summons the Demon Lord.

Field Advice

Break the cage, control the doorway, then count the wings. If the number seems too low, look above you.

Kael'Vorr's Note

Never underestimate a creature simply because you can pick it up. It may be holding your keys.
